reason: Internal only, read-only, no model and no behaviour change: `nora measure participation` computes the four measures that grade the ambient path against something other than its own opinion (design/culture-tier/02-measurement, step 2). Today the verdict IS the measurement — a model agreeing with the instruction someone wrote it is not evidence about the room, and a refusal is indistinguishable from health in every log the system keeps, which is how a 1% admission rate went unremarked for days. The four are: a note passed its anchor day while open and she never raised it; the gate refused a room while she held an open note born there; a human tagged her shortly after a refusal; she spoke unprompted and the next human line did not engage. Two are labelled by her own store and two by human behaviour, so neither pair is self-attesting. Every measure carries its own ceiling in its output rather than a shared footnote, because they are blind to different things. The refusal half comes from a separate script against Prometheus rather than a flag, because a counter that resets with the process is a much weaker instrument than a durable row, and the command refuses a refusal file that does not span the window asked for — a short list makes the refusal-side measures look clean, which is also what they would say if nothing had been refused. First live run found three of seven anchored notes had passed their day unraised. It also caught a unit error in its own first draft: anchor_date is a YYYYMMDD calendar day while every other instant is epoch milliseconds, and compared raw it classified every anchored note as expired. Nothing a member of a room can observe.
